text.title: python Examples
text.summary: Worked code for the five areas the rules cover: Poetry project setup, Django patterns, FastAPI patterns, pytest patterns, and asyncio patterns.

section.title: Project setup with Poetry
section.p: Poetry initialization, pyproject.toml layout, dependency groups, venv activation, and Docker integration.

section.title: Setup steps

example.code:
# New project poetry new my-project && cd my-project
# Add production and dev dependencies poetry add django fastapi poetry add --group dev pytest pytest-django pytest-cov mypy ruff
# Install from lock file (CI) poetry install --no-root
# Activate virtual environment poetry shell
# Run without activating poetry run pytest poetry run python manage.py migrate
# Export for Docker poetry export -f requirements.txt --output requirements.txt --without-hashes

section.reference: Minimal pyproject.toml with dev group and tool stubs

example.code: # Install and pin Python version for project pyenv install 3.11.7 cd my-project pyenv local 3.11.7 poetry env use $(pyenv which python) poetry install

FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app RUN pip install poetry COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock ./ RUN poetry config virtualenvs.create false \ && poetry install --no-interaction --only main COPY . . CMD ["python", "main.py"]

section.title: Django patterns
section.p: BaseModel with UUID and timestamps, services layer for business logic, thin views, serializers, and admin with fieldsets.

example.code:
from rest_framework.views import APIView from rest_framework.response import Response from rest_framework import status from . import services from .serializers import CreateUserRequest, UserResponse
class UserCreateView(APIView): def post(self, request): serializer = CreateUserRequest(data=request.data) serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True) user = services.create_user(**serializer.validated_data) return Response(UserResponse(user).data, status=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)

section.title: FastAPI patterns
section.p: FastAPI app with lifespan, Depends() injection, Pydantic schemas, and background tasks. See python-fastapi/ for the full methodology.

section.title: pytest patterns
section.p: conftest fixtures, factory fixtures, mocking with patch, parametrize for edge cases, and Django DB integration tests.

example.code:
import pytest from apps.users.validators import validate_email
@pytest.mark.parametrize("email,expected", [ ("user@example.com", True), ("user.name@example.co.uk", True), ("invalid", False), ("@example.com", False), ("", False), ]) def test_validate_email(email: str, expected: bool) -> None: assert validate_email(email) == expected

section.title: asyncio patterns
section.p: asyncio.gather for concurrent I/O, TaskGroup for structured concurrency, Semaphore for rate limiting, and timeouts.

example.note: Use asyncio.gather() for independent concurrent I/O operations. Sequential await calls run one at a time; gather runs them concurrently, reducing total latency proportionally.

example.code: async def process_batch(items: list[str]) -> list[str]: results = [] async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: for item in items: task = tg.create_task(process_item(item)) # All tasks completed; collect results return [task.result() for task in ...]

# asyncio.wait_for (all Python versions) try: result = await asyncio.wait_for(slow_operation(), timeout=2.0) except asyncio.TimeoutError: ...
# asyncio.timeout context manager (Python 3.11+) async with asyncio.timeout(2.0): result = await slow_operation()
